papers.title: Human Versus AI Feedback for Aligning Large Language Models: A Comparative Review of RLHF and RLAIF
papers.summary: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences commonly relies on reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), which depends on costly preference labels collected from human annotators. Reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) replaces some or all of these labels with judgments produced by an LLM. This paper presents a focused comparative review of RLHF and RLAIF based on twelve core publications. papers.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for reservoir cascade release scheduling: a climate-analytics evaluation of downstream low-flow equity under forecast uncertainty
papers.summary: Cascade reservoir operators must release water under uncertain inflow forecasts while satisfying competing demands for hydropower, irrigation and downstream environmental flows. The framework is formalised as a constrained Markov game with a lexicographic objective: maximise energy revenue subject to a probabilistic low-flow equity constraint at downstream reaches. papers.title: Evaluating Xception with Multitask Self-Supervised Learning for AI-Generated Image and Deepfake Video Detection
papers.summary: This study evaluates an Xception-based Multitask Self-Supervised Learning (MSSL) framework for detecting real and synthetic visual content across image and video modalities. papers.title: A scoping review mapping the role of Husserlian phenomenology in artificial intelligence research
papers.summary: AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. papers.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
papers.summary: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. papers.title: A Computer Vision-Based Framework for Multilevel Egg Fertility Classification Using L*a*b* Color Segmentation, Wavelet Texture Features, and Support Vector Machine
papers.summary: Egg fertility assessment is essential for improving hatchery efficiency, reducing incubation costs, and minimizing resource waste caused by infertile eggs. This study aims to develop a computer vision-based framework for three-level egg fertility classification, namely Highly Fertile, Fertile, and Infertile.
